column1: # Every metric family the Python api registers, with its Go status: the
# route-counter inventory. Two venue tests check it by execution:
# TestCounterParityVenueOracle (every import-time family is named with its
# type; ported and partial rows are the counters it compares) and
# TestPythonMetricsTableSweepVenueOracle (runs the Python api's route tests
# with a plugin that records the route each family fires under).
#   type   lazy:<type> = registered only when its code first runs, so absent
#   routes the ";"-separated routes ("<METHODS> <path>") the family fired
#          under in the sweep, plus the route the parity oracle drives it
#          through; "-" when it fired under none. The sweep requires exactly
#   status (the sweep checks each against the dho api's route set)
#     ported           = compared by the oracle; the dho api serves every listed route
#     partial          = compared by the oracle; the dho api serves some listed routes
#                        and does not count it on the others (note)
#     route-missing    = the dho api serves a listed route and does not count it yet
#     unreached        = the source fires it from a route (note), but no Python test
#                        fires it under a route, so no route is listed
#     route-not-ported = fired by a Python route the dho api does not serve
#     other-go-service = fired by a route another Go service serves (the query-api)
#     worker           = fired by job/worker code, not an api route
#     python-only      = Python-api machinery with no Go counterpart to port
#     retired          = fired by code that no longer runs (Celery)
#     unused           = no caller left in the Python source; the sweep never fires it
